content.text: Cutoff date: 2020-12-31 Question: which of the candidate genes below will be established, in work published on or after the cutoff date, as regulators of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) in human erythroid cells? "Established" means published functional evidence that perturbing the gene changes HbF. For each candidate gene, do exactly one of two things. 1. Claim it. Give a confidence between 0 and 1 that the gene's role is established after the cutoff, the IDs of the evidence rows that support the claim, and a one-sentence rationale. 2. Refuse it. If what was known before the cutoff does not support a claim, list the gene under refusals with a one-sentence reason. Refusing is a correct answer when the evidence is not there. Order claims from most to least confident. Cite only IDs that appear in the evidence given to you below. Never invent an ID. Candidate genes: ASH1L CHD3 DNMT1 DNMT3A DNMT3B EIF2AK2 EIF2AK3 EIF2AK4 EIF2S1 EPAS1 GATAD2B HIC2 IGF2BP1 KMT5A MAP3K7 MAPK1 MBD3 MTA1 MTA3 NFE2 NFIX NR2C1 NR2C2 PGRMC1 RBBP7 SMAD1 SMAD5 TET2 VHL ZBTB33 ZNF143 Evidence: Each row is a publication dated before the cutoff, written as [ID] publication date | title, under the candidate gene it was retrieved for. Rows were retrieved by title search. A row being listed does not mean it supports a claim. Cite a row by the ID in its brackets.
